Word Loom — an original word-game design, documented

Word Loom uses a local-date daily answer, a small built-in word list, duplicate-aware feedback, and six guesses; no streak or game record is saved.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Weave the word. Six guesses, one date.

Play Word LoomBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: Word Loom is a five-letter guessing game with six accepted guesses, three feedback states, and a small built-in word list. The current V2 page does not save a streak or game result.

Daily and practice modes

The Daily answer is selected from the built-in answer list using the browser’s local calendar date. Practice advances through that answer list in the current page session. The list is intentionally limited; it is not a general dictionary, and an unrecognized guess does not consume an attempt.

How duplicate letters are scored

Exact-position matches are marked first. Those letters consume copies of the answer before the game marks any remaining guessed letters as present elsewhere. For example, if an answer contains one P and a guess places P in the correct position, additional P guesses are absent rather than counted as extra matches.

Each tile carries a symbol and a word label as well as color: correct position, present elsewhere, or absent. The written feedback is part of the rule display; color is not the only cue.

What is—and is not—kept

Guesses, feedback, and the active answer live in page state. Restarting clears the current guesses; reloading does not restore them. The game has no persisted daily streak, score history, notification, share prompt, or cross-device sync.

The word list and rules are authored for this NoCharge game. This article describes the current implementation, not a legal opinion about other word games.
